result.summary: This pull request introduces a vectorized ChaCha20 implementation using GCC and Clang compiler vector built-ins rather than hand-written assembly. It calculates multiple cipher blocks concurrently, yielding a 2x to 3x throughput improvement across x86-64 and AArch64 platforms.
result.problem: ChaCha20 processing consumes a noticeable fraction of CPU time on the node's network thread when using BIP324 transport encryption. Speeding up this primitive lowers peer-to-peer CPU overhead and shortens compute-bound sync phases.

result.card: PR 34083 adds an initial vectorized ChaCha20 implementation using compiler built-ins, achieving a 2-3x throughput improvement across x86-64 and AArch64. This reduces CPU usage on the network thread under BIP324 transport encryption and yields measurable speedups during initial block download. Concept support is strong, but the PR is currently paused in draft while waiting on the author to address a changes-requested review regarding hardware regressions, commit restructuring, and fuzzing coverage.
